+#pragma once
+// The AVX-512 (the CPU's 512-bit vector instruction set) QK score reader of the
+// K VNNI layout (h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp). It serves partial pages, hosts
+// without AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions, the tile instruction set) and the
+// AMX kill switch (TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1). No AMX instruction runs here. So any
+// translation unit may include it. The layout itself, who writes it and who
+// reads it are described in Note [K VNNI storage] (in kv_cache.hpp).
+//
+// Words used here: bf16 is the 16-bit brain floating-point format. fp16 is the
+// 16-bit IEEE half format. fp32 is the 32-bit IEEE single format. VDPBF16PS is
+// the AVX-512 instruction that multiplies bf16 pairs and adds them in fp32.
+
+#include <cstddef>
+#include <cstdint>
+#include <cstring>
+#include <immintrin.h>
+#include <type_traits>
+
+#include "common/attributes.hpp"
+#include "common/numerics/bf16.hpp"
+#include "common/numerics/fp16.hpp"
+#include "tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp"
+
+namespace tron::k_vnni {
+
+// One accumulator register per query head of the group (qk_group).
+inline constexpr size_t MAX_KV_MUL_16 = 16;
+
+// qk_group is a template. It is instantiated only for VNNI slots, which
+// kv_cache.hpp rejects outside the 16-lane build. So it needs no lane guard,
+// and its qualified name stays declared for the discarded branch of
+// self_attention.hpp's layout `if constexpr`.
+
+// Scores of one query group against the live tokens of one page, read from
+// the VNNI plane with AVX-512. s[h * s_stride + t] = q_h . K_t (UNSCALED) for
+// every token t whose bit is set in `live`. The other entries of s are left
+// untouched (the caller keeps them at -inf). The K storage of a token whose
+// bit is clear is never read (masked loads). So unwritten tokens cannot
+// change the result. Token lanes: one 64-byte load supplies one dimension pair
+// of 16 tokens. The query's dimension pair is broadcast. VDPBF16PS accumulates 16
+// scores at once. So there is no horizontal reduction and no per-token gather.
+// k_page is the page's packed K plane as its typed view (page::k_packed). This
+// reader is one of the two layout-specific readers allowed to take the plane
+// address. q points at kv_mul rows of 128 values (the group's heads, row
+// stride 128).
+//   bf16 q: exact bf16 x bf16 products added in fp32 by VDPBF16PS. This is the
+//     same instruction the row-major dotter<bf16, 128> uses. Only the order of
+//     the fp32 adds differs (see Note [AMX attention dispatch]).
+//   float q: the stored bf16 K values are widened to fp32 exactly (a shift).
+//     They are then multiplied by the fp32 query with FMA (fused multiply-add),
+//     as dotter<float, 128> does.
+//   fp16 q: widened to fp32 once per call, then the float path.
+template <size_t kv_mul, typename q_scalar>
+TRON(inline)
+void qk_group(k_vnni_view<const bf16, PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> k_page,
+    const q_scalar* q,
+    uint64_t live,
+    float* s,
+    size_t s_stride) noexcept {
+  static_assert(
+      kv_mul >= 1 && kv_mul <= MAX_KV_MUL_16, "one accumulator register per head");
body:
**[P2] Preserve software attention for groups larger than 16 query heads**

`TRON_K_VNNI` (the packed K storage option) selects every 128-dimension K/V head, regardless of how many query heads share it. The existing geometry contract accepts `attention_geometry{32, {1, 128}}`: 32 query heads sharing one K/V head. I instantiated `apply_page_tok` (the production per-page attention function) for this geometry with float queries. It compiles with the option disabled, but enabling it fails here with `32 <= 16` through the call at `self_attention.hpp:1869`. This rejects a previously supported software-attention shape even when AMX is unavailable.

Please process larger query groups in chunks of at most 16 heads, or otherwise retain a software path for these valid geometries. A compile check through `apply_page_tok` with this shape would catch the regression. The existing oversized-group fallback test uses 64 dimensions per head, so it does not exercise this branch.

body:
Confirmed and fixed in 977826a272, with the tests completed in 76ef81e2fc.

The cause: `k_vnni::qk_group` (the AVX-512 reader of the VNNI K layout) kept one accumulator register per query head and rejected a group of more than 16 heads with a `static_assert`. `TRON_K_VNNI` selects every 128-dimension K/V head, so `attention_geometry{32, {1, 128}}` reached that assert through `apply_page_tok`. The limit came from PR #4424; this port kept it.

The fix: `qk_group` scores a group wider than 16 heads in passes of 16 (the first 16 heads, then the rest, which may split again). Every head's scores are its own accumulation. So the split changes no head's add order. A group of at most 16 heads takes the same single pass as before. An independent check compared the split reader against a single-pass copy of the previous kernel for 17, 20, 32 and 33 heads with bf16, float and fp16 queries, 26 live masks each: no mismatching score.

Tests added:
- `t_k_vnni_layout`: the reader-versus-dotter case runs for 4, 20 and 32 query heads (one pass, an uneven split, two full passes), with bf16, float and fp16 queries, the same masks, NaN poison and tolerance as before.
- `t_llama_unit`: a case that instantiates `apply_page_tok` for 32 query heads on one 128-dimension K/V head in both builds (with and without `TRON_K_VNNI`) and runs it on a page whose query mask excludes every token. At the previous head it does not compile with the option on.

Verified at 76ef81e2fc: both tests pass on claude-box (AVX-512 host) with `TRON_K_VNNI` on and off, and on delphi-3bda (real AMX, VNNI build with ingest models): `t_k_vnni_layout` 1011650 assertions / 5 cases, `t_llama_unit` 246843 / 46, `t_amx_numerics` 12813 / 5, `t_amx_dispatch_dtype`, `t_heterogeneous_scheduler` and `t_phase1_integration` all pass.

Verified the fix and reviewed both new commits through `76ef81e2fc`. The original production `apply_page_tok` compile probe (32 query heads sharing one 128-dimension K/V head, float queries) now passes with `TRON_K_VNNI` enabled and disabled.

An independent reader probe also passed for 1, 16, 17, 20, 32, 33 and 64 query heads with bf16, float and fp16 inputs. It checked nine live-token masks, NaN-poisoned excluded rows, and an output stride of 80 floats. Every live score matched an independent scalar reference exactly for the chosen exactly representable inputs. Excluded scores and row padding remained unchanged.

The split preserves query offsets, output strides and each head's accumulation order. The new production-instantiation and numerical tests cover the reported failure. No new actionable findings in the four changed files. Full suites and AMX/FPGA hardware tests were not rerun. This addresses the original finding; resolving.

**[P3] Test saved rows without requiring this exact work partition**

These assertions, continuing through line 3670, require nine units and every current boundary. For example, merging the first three units around the no-KV job at offset 8 preserves the saved rows: `store_k_block` already skips such jobs within a run. That valid refactor would fail this test despite satisfying the existing `check(before)` checks for every expected and untouched row.

Please remove the exact unit-count/boundary assertions and retain the outcome checks. The repository's test policy requires an identifiable consumer contract for assertions about internal fields and ordering; this particular partition is not required by the consumers.

**[P3] Give the added layout constants names required by the C++ guide**

The new K scratch uses an unnamed fixed alignment. Please express it with a named constant such as `K_SCRATCH_ALIGNMENT_64`. The same issue occurs in the new conversion scratch at `model.hpp:2899` and the transpose stage sizes/offsets at `tensor/k_vnni.hpp:317–335`. Naming the pair, quarter and half widths would make the shuffle structure easier to follow and satisfy the guide's rule for fixed values.

This is a nonblocking coding-guide finding; I found no incorrect alignment or transpose result. Keep the cleanup scoped to added or modified code.
